name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 11 points on the partisan baseline
Incumbent Tim Kennedy is running with a large cash advantage ($2.3M raised, $1.2M on hand)
Republican Dennis Hannon shows no reported fundraising or outside support
Prediction markets price Kennedy near 97% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Kennedy: an 11-point Democratic lean, incumbency, and a dominant fundraising edge against an opponent with no visible financial backing. Markets price this as effectively decided, so the forecast stays near the baseline with only a slight trim for the absence of polling.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Kennedy underperforming the district's lean, or unexpected outside spending for Hannon, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Buffalo-area district that voted about 11 points Democratic at the presidential level. He enters the race with a substantial financial advantage, having raised over $2.3 million and holding $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Dennis Hannon reports no fundraising on file and no outside groups are active in the race.

Prediction markets give Kennedy roughly a 97 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the seat as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, Kennedy's incumbency, and the money gap, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
